title: Molecular-Genetic Basis of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH).
authors: Okot, Mark; Ahmed, Aneesa; Wright, Colin W; Nasim, Md Talat
one_liner_zh: 该文是肺动脉高压分子遗传学综述，虽提及转录因子和AI技术，但核心是疾病遗传机制而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive, fatal disease of the pulmonary vasculature characterized by obliterative remodeling of small pulmonary arteries, leading to sustained elevation of pulmonary vascular resistance, right ventricular failure, and premature death. The diagnostic gold standard remains right heart catheterization, requiring a mean pulmonary artery pressure greater than 20 mmHg at rest, a pulmonary arterial wedge pressure of 15 mmHg or below, and a pulmonary vascular resistance exceeding 2 Wood units. PAH is an autosomal dominant disorder with markedly incomplete penetrance of approximately 20-30%, indicating that germline mutations alone are insufficient to cause disease. Disease manifestation requires additional "second hits", including chronic hypoxia, systemic inflammation, hemodynamic stress, hormonal influences, and common genetic modifiers such as single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). This genetic and environmental complexity underpins the broad clinical heterogeneity observed across PAH subtypes, which include idiopathic PAH, heritable PAH, and disease associated with connective tissue disorders, HIV infection, portal hypertension, congenital heart disease, schistosomiasis, and drug or toxin exposure. This review provides a comprehensive and critical appraisal of the molecular-genetic architecture of PAH. Thirty genes have now been implicated in disease pathogenesis, spanning seven functional categories: receptors of the TGF-beta/BMP signaling family (BMPR2, ACVRL1, ENG, BMPR1B); circulating BMP ligands (GDF2, BMP10); transcription factors (TBX4, SOX17, KLF4, FOXF1, SMAD1, SMAD4, SMAD9); membrane and polyamine transporters (ATP13A3, AQP1); potassium channel regulators (KCNA5, KCNK3, ABCC8); metabolic and mitochondrial genes (EIF2AK4, NFU1, GGCX); signaling receptors and structural proteins (NOTCH3, KDR, CAV1, PLEKHH2); vasoactive and extracellular matrix regulators (KLK1, CBLN2, CD248); and epigenetic regulators (TET2, TOPBP1). Among these, BMPR2 is the dominant contributor, accounting for 53-86% of heritable PAH and 14-35% of idiopathic cases. The remaining genes each account for fewer than 5% of cases individually, collectively reflecting a broad landscape of rare and ultra-rare genetic contributions. For each gene, we critically evaluate the strength of genetic evidence, pathogenic mechanisms, degree of mechanistic resolution, and clinical relevance. We further discuss the contribution of emerging technologies, including whole-genome sequencing, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, multi-omics integration, iPSC-derived vascular models, and artificial intelligence, to expanding the PAH genetic architecture beyond single-gene discovery. A key theme across this landscape is convergence: despite mechanistic diversity at the gene level, most PAH-associated variants ultimately impair endothelial quiescence, promote smooth muscle proliferation, and drive apoptosis resistance through disruption of BMP signaling amplitude, transcriptional stability, ion channel homeostasis, metabolic integrity, or epigenetic regulation. This convergence supports both a unified therapeutic rationale and a precision medicine framework for genotype-stratified intervention in PAH.
abstract_zh: 肺动脉高压（pulmonary arterial hypertension, PAH）是一种进行性、致命性的肺血管疾病，其特征为小肺动脉的闭塞性重塑，导致肺血管阻力持续升高、右心室衰竭和过早死亡。诊断金标准仍为右心导管检查，要求静息状态下平均肺动脉压大于20 mmHg，肺动脉楔压≤15 mmHg，且肺血管阻力超过2 Wood单位。PAH是一种常染色体显性遗传病，外显率显著不完全，约为20-30%，表明仅凭种系突变不足以致病。疾病表现需额外的“二次打击”，包括慢性缺氧、全身性炎症、血流动力学应激、激素影响以及常见遗传修饰因子，如单核苷酸多态性（single-nucleotide polymorphisms, SNPs）。这种遗传和环境复杂性构成了PAH各亚型所观察到的广泛临床异质性的基础，这些亚型包括特发性PAH、遗传性PAH，以及与结缔组织病、HIV感染、门脉高压、先天性心脏病、血吸虫病及药物或毒素暴露相关的PAH。本综述对PAH的分子遗传学架构进行了全面且批判性的评估。目前已有30个基因被证实参与疾病发病机制，涵盖七个功能类别：TGF-β/BMP信号家族受体（BMPR2、ACVRL1、ENG、BMPR1B）；循环BMP配体（GDF2、BMP10）；转录因子（TBX4、SOX17、KLF4、FOXF1、SMAD1、SMAD4、SMAD9）；膜及多胺转运体（ATP13A3、AQP1）；钾通道调节因子（KCNA5、KCNK3、ABCC8）；代谢及线粒体基因（EIF2AK4、NFU1、GGCX）；信号受体及结构蛋白（NOTCH3、KDR、CAV1、PLEKHH2）；血管活性及细胞外基质调节因子（KLK1、CBLN2、CD248）；以及表观遗传调节因子（TET2、TOPBP1）。其中，BMPR2是主要贡献者，占遗传性PAH的53-86%和特发性病例的14-35%。其余基因各自占病例比例不足5%，共同反映了罕见及超罕见遗传贡献的广泛格局。针对每个基因，我们批判性地评估了遗传证据强度、致病机制、机制解析程度及临床相关性。我们进一步讨论了新兴技术，包括全基因组测序、单细胞及空间转录组学、多组学整合、iPSC来源血管模型及人工智能，在将PAH遗传架构扩展至单基因发现之外的贡献。贯穿这一格局的关键主题是汇聚性：尽管基因水平上机制多样，大多数PAH相关变异最终通过干扰BMP信号幅度、转录稳定性、离子通道稳态、代谢完整性或表观遗传调控，损害内皮静息状态，促进平滑肌增殖，并驱动凋亡抵抗。这种汇聚性既支持统一的治疗原理，也为PAH中基于基因型分层的干预提供了精准医学框架。
